lead_headline: Weekend restaurant sweep: 3 new leads break the freeze — Wapos Cantina in Rosedale, Mendocino Farms at Union Station, and Powered By Besitos food truck closure in West Colfax

restaurant.blurb: 3 leads since Friday: Wapos Cantina opened in Rosedale (former El Tepehuan), Mendocino Farms debuted at Union Station (third Denver location), Powered By Besitos food truck closed in West Colfax.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications — the freeze extends to 38 days. Not a single bar, restaurant, or retail license filing since early June. The post-holiday Monday typically restarts the licensing pipeline, but the drought persists. The 12,325-license database historically processes 2-4 weekly applications even during summer slowdowns. This six-week void now marks the longest recorded application silence. Whether driven by capital constraints, state administrative backlogs, or structural shifts in hospitality investment appetite, the freeze shows no thaw. The next filing will reset a clock on a licensing paralysis without precedent in the modern database era.

reputation.blurb: 0 mentions yesterday — the July 4 holiday extended into a silent Sunday. The week closes at 71 mentions across 18 sources, up 15% from last week's 62. Facebook leads with 23 citations, Reddit contributes 18, X.com adds 6, Instagram 5, Hoodline 3. Google News RSS captured 69 of 71 discoveries. Top stories: Broncos headquarters investment, Inspirato sponsorship exit, Colorado mayor's shelter nights. The holiday weekend typically compresses citation velocity. Monday's resumption will clarify whether the uptrend holds or last week's surge was a temporary spike before seasonal summer decline.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat since Friday (3 new, 3 canceled) holds MTD at +9 (+1.8/day). 90-day net: +117. The weekend delivered zero net movement after Friday's −1, marking four consecutive days without positive momentum (Wed −1, Thu −1, Fri −1, weekend flat). The explosive June 29-30 surge (+17 in 48 hours) now looks increasingly like an outlier. July's +1.8/day pace still exceeds YTD baseline (+1.3/day), but barely. The 7-day window (+26 net) masks the recent stall — remove the June 29-30 spike and the trend flattens to near-zero. Holiday weekend timing clouds the signal, but the pattern mirrors the pre-surge June doldrums that preceded a −9 week.
